 ## Search results
Evidence supports testing the objective before increasing NextItNet depth. [On the Effectiveness of Sampled Softmax (2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) connects sampled-softmax optimization to ranking performance and emphasizes temperature: excessively hard negatives can dominate gradients. [Scalable Cross-Entropy (RecSys 2024)](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26) approximates catalog-wide CE by selectively computing informative high-scoring outputs. These results motivate multi-negative candidate discrimination, but sampled CE remains a surrogate, not direct HR@10 optimization.

Sampling details matter. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that the always-present positive requires different treatment from sampled negatives when deriving importance corrections. [Sequential negative-sampling experiments (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) find substantial dataset-dependent tradeoffs across uniform, popularity, in-batch and adaptive samplers. Neither high model scores nor missing interactions establish that an item is truly negative. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) addresses false negatives using a teacher, making its mechanism unsuitable for this constraint.

Practical hypothesis: retain one NextItNet per category; compare the baseline against temperature-controlled multi-negative softmax, then a uniform/semi-hard mixture mined by that same network. Exclude padding, targets and known training positives; deduplicate candidates. Warm up with uniform negatives, then introduce moderate hardness rather than always selecting maxima. These are proposed experiments, not established improvements or reliable false-negative identification. Use training histories only for filtering and sampling, preserve the pinned evaluator, and select by macro validation HR@10. No teacher, additional predictor or inference score fusion is needed.

---

The search found related mechanisms, but no verified 2023–2026 NextItNet extension directly establishing input-dependent context resets. [FADC (CVPR 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05369) adjusts dilation per spatial position using local frequency information; useful architectural inspiration, with evidence from vision rather than recommendation. [DyS4Rec (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2025.107134) learns to skip irrelevant historical interactions in sequential recommendation. [Mamba (2023/2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00752) demonstrates input-dependent propagation and forgetting, offering a selection principle transferable as a hypothesis without replacing NextItNet’s convolutional backbone.

Proposed adaptation: gate individual causal convolution taps using the current prefix representation and the corresponding historical feature, before summation. This selects information within each receptive field rather than merely weighting fixed-depth outputs. A stronger reset variant could attenuate a tap by the product of learned retention gates across intervening positions, suppressing paths crossing inferred context boundaries. Both are proposed mechanisms, not established results from these papers; retain causal inputs, padding masks, residual connections, and one jointly trained network per category.

Controls should compare against parameter-matched ungated convolutions, uniform gates, learned input-independent tap weights, and fixed recent-history windows. Shuffle gates across examples or replace them with their means to test whether input dependence matters. Evaluate older-history removal separately from corruption: stronger sensitivity to recent perturbations establishes reliance, not harm from older context. Report macro validation HR@10 alongside gate variability, effective lag usage, and results by history length; keep seeds, training budget, and candidate sets fixed.

---

Recent research supports text as complementary item information, but provides limited direct evidence for a lightweight, from-scratch text encoder inside NextItNet. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines textual item representations with sequential modeling and reports content ablations; however, it uses BERT, a SASRec-derived backbone, and reviews, with reviews contributing most. Its gains therefore do not establish that titles/descriptions alone will improve this constrained setting. [DWSRec (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28786) shows that the geometry of pretrained text embeddings affects recommendation quality, reinforcing that semantic similarity requires adaptation to recommendation objectives.

A constraint-compatible hypothesis is to retain [NextItNet’s dilated convolutional residual backbone](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163), adding randomly initialized token embeddings with masked mean pooling or a small text CNN over titles/descriptions. Project and gate these features into item-ID embeddings; jointly train the entire network using next-item supervision and use the same item representation for candidate scoring. This is a proposed adaptation, not a verified result from the retrieved papers. Preserve item-specific ID capacity so shared wording does not collapse distinct products. Compare ID-only, title-only augmentation, and title-plus-description augmentation through separate single-model trials using macro validation HR@10; retain one checkpoint per category.
